newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco stadium bond lags in voter poll.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco stadium bond lags in voter poll.

text.p: A $100 million bond measure for a proposed San Francisco stadium complex has made no headway with voters and now trails by nine percentage points, according to a poll published Tuesday.
The San Francisco Chronicle poll of 600 San Franciscans found that 47 percent oppose the stadium plan, 38 percent support it and 15 percent are undecided.

San Francisco residents will vote June 3 on the $100 million lease revenue bond measure. The bond funds would help to finance the city's share of the proposed $525 million San Francisco 49ers football stadium and shopping complex.
The Chronicle poll was conducted last weekend.
A joint San Francisco KPIX-TV and KCBS radio poll released Monday also showed the stadium measure trailing, but by only four percentage points.
An earlier Chronicle poll had found the measure trailing by eight percentage points.
